integrity: Nested same-side neighborhoods imply that a solid-locating code can omit at most one vertex from each bipartition side. Every cross-side two-vertex complement is then solid-locating except the two leaf-corner pairs whose omitted leaf has empty identifying set. For self-location-domination, the standard forced-codeword criterion forces all vertices except a_1 and b_n, and the resulting complement-two code has the required singleton closed-neighborhood intersections for n at least three.
scientific_limitations: The theorem treats thin half graphs rather than arbitrary chain graphs with repeated twin classes.
The n=2 boundary has different self-locating behavior and is excluded from the common formula.
Finite exhaustive verification covers n from two through eight and is corroborative only.
A differently phrased or non-indexed chain-graph treatment may exist.
title: Self- and solid-location-domination of half graphs
